To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultrasonic treatment of glass carbon in water is an effective method to produce nanoparticles, but only if the sonication is carried out in a specific reactor.

the ultrasonic treatment of glass carbon in water is a simple and cheap method to obtain carbon nanoparticles, which are stable in suspension in water and can be used as a precursor for carbon nanotubes.
sonication of glassycarbon in water leads to the preparation of stable suspensions of nanoparticles, which are easily separated from the sonicated particles by decantation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the ultrasonic treatment of glass-like carbon particles in water.

the preparation of stable suspensions of glassy carbon nanoparticles by sonication of glass carbon microparticles in water, and with the multiscale structural changes of the irradiated particles as a function of sonication time.
the preparation and characterization of glassy carbon nanoparticles by ultrasound.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sonication time, the sonication power, the sonication reactor geometry, and the particle size, all have a significant influence on the yield of the preparation of nanoparticles, their structure and their chemical properties.

the ultrasonic treatment of glassycarbon particles in water allows the preparation of stable suspensions of glassy carbon nanoparticles with a high yield (1-3wt%), and that these suspensions can be separated from the sediment particles.

the sonication in water of glassy carbon leads to a progressive amorphization of the material and to the production of nanoparticles with disordered aromatic structure, but with a closed mesoporous network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ultrasonic treatment of carbon materials in water allows preparing stable suspensions of nanoparticles, with a high degree of amorphization and a strong loss of the mesoporosity.
the ultrasonic treatment of glassycarbon in water is a simple way to prepare stable aqueous suspensions of carbonnanoparticles with a controlled size and a controlled degree of disorder.
the ultrasonic treatment in water of glassy carbon particles leads to a strong amorphisation of the carbon material and to a loss of the nanostructure of the mesopores.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ultrasonic treatment in water is a very efficient way to produce nanoparticles of glassy carbons from micrometric particles of glassy carbids.
the ultrasonic treatment of glass carbon particles in water allows preparing stable suspensions of glassy carbon nanoparticles, easily separable from the sedimented micrometric particles.
ultrasonic treatment can be a promising method to prepare carbon nanomaterials.
